The Hebrew עִם phrase is an adjunct of the infinitive clause (to grave gravings with the skilful men), not the predicate of a verbless clause, so no construction supplies a copula (rule 20 test: the Hebrew made no predication 'the man is with the skilful men'); the italic to be is a supplied infinitival copula and one added run (rule 2). Giving to be to עִם under rule 49 was the accepted reading.
